 Dominican-Born Man Living In Massachusetts Steals Puerto Rican Citizen’s Identity, Pockets $24,000 in SNAP Benefits 
 Also available in Português / Español 
 Share 
 Advertisement 
  Erpawi Roque Collado, a 54-year-old Lawful Permanent Resident born in the Dominican Republic, pleaded guilty in federal court today to unlawfully obtaining Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and theft of government money.
 Collado admitted to stealing the identity of a U.S. citizen from Puerto Rico and using it to fraudulently collect $24,128 in SNAP benefits from the Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance between December 2016 and May 2025.
 Advertisement 
 U.S. District Court Judge Brian E. Murphy scheduled sentencing for January 14, 2027. Collado was indicted on April 23, 2026.
 The charge of unlawfully obtaining SNAP benefits carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine. The charge of theft of government money carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine. Sentences will be determined by the court under the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and applicable federal statutes.
